response.claim_ceiling: May claim: (a) standard isomorphisms su(2)~Im(H), G2=Aut(O), F4=Aut(Albert), and the known exceptional chain; (b) that a sim can host these algebras as explicit multiplication tables or matrix representations; (c) that multi-engine/Choi/IGT layers are the natural place to look for relational structure. May not claim: that the existing engine/axes system already is O/Albert/E8, that dimension or generator counts prove the identification, that exceptional math is dynamically load-bearing without measured equivariance, or any physical/computational universality beyond the finite checked representations.
kill_controls: Replace O by H, C, or a random 8-dim algebra with generic structure constants; Aut dim and exceptional identities must collapse.
Replace H3(O) by H3(H), H3(C), or M_3(R)/M_3(C); F4-type stabilizer and 27-dim cubic form must fail.
Force associativity or use only matrix-gate engines; nonassociative/Jordan signatures must disappear.
Dimension/character kill: if claimed G2/F4/E6 action does not reproduce known irrep dimensions or Killing-form signatures on the nose, reject.
Shuffled or noise-corrupted structure constants: any 'exceptional load-bearing' signal that survives is false positive.
Single-engine vs multi-engine ablation: exceptional features claimed at axes 7–12 must vanish when engines are decoupled or Choi layer is replaced by product of independent channels.
response.likely_next_sim: Finite, fully explicit: (1) single-engine baseline = random SU(2)/quaternion multiplications vs Pauli conjugation, track associators=0 and dim=3 Im(H); (2) one-rung lift = 8-dim real algebra with fixed octonion structure constants, measure Aut-dimension (target 14) and associator identities under random basis change; (3) Albert probe = 27-dim Hermitian 3×3 over that algebra, check Jordan identity and cubic norm preservation under candidate F4 generators; (4) multi-engine/Choi layer = 1–3 qubit CP maps (Choi matrices), attempt to embed or project candidate exceptional actions and score equivariance residual; all runs with exact arithmetic or high-precision float and seed-controlled randomness.
response.notes_for_codex: Track every object by real dimension, multiplication table or structure constants, and explicit group action (matrices or code). Prefer finite exact checks over narrative. Separate 'we embedded the algebra' from 'the sim discovered the algebra'. Reject any claim that rests only on counting 7, 8, 14, 26/27, 52, etc. Next code should output pass/fail tables for the kill controls above; if they do not cleanly kill the non-exceptional baselines, the exceptional story is not yet load-bearing.
strong_points: su(2) ≅ Im(H) and single-qubit Bloch/Pauli structure is standard and clean.
G2 = Aut(O), F4 = Aut(H3(O)/Albert), and the Freudenthal/magic-square lift G2→F4→E6→E7→E8 is legitimate classical structure theory.
Treating multi-engine relations (including game-theoretic payoffs/interactions) as living one level above single-engine algebra is conceptually coherent.
Choi/superoperator layer correctly sits at the CP-map / open-system level rather than pure-state single-qubit level.
response.verdict: Algebraically grounded scaffolding with known exceptional-series facts, but heavy overclaim and category risk when mapped to engines/axes/Choi/IGT without explicit isomorphisms, representations, or dimension-checked embeddings.
weak_points: No concrete functor or faithful representation is given that turns an 'engine' into H or a field-of-engines into H3(O)/Freudenthal data; analogy ≠ realization.
Dimension mismatches are ignored: dim_R H=4, O=8, H3(O)=27; g2=14, f4=52, e6=78, e7=133, e8=248. Counts of axes/generators alone never establish the Lie or Jordan structure.
Axes 7–12 / Choi layer is underspecified: superoperators on n qubits live in dim 4^n (Choi), not automatically in Albert or E-series modules.
Nonassociativity of O and the cubic Jordan product on H3(O) are not free; most gate-model or matrix-engine sims stay associative/matrix and will not spontaneously produce them.
IGT/game theory as 'relations among engines' is a modeling choice, not a derived theorem from the exceptional chain.
Category error risk: symmetry groups of algebras ≠ dynamical symmetry of a sim, and 'shadow' language does not substitute for equivariant maps or character tables.
